title: Sell Mineral Rights in Atlasburg, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Atlasburg, PA | Get an Offer
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Atlasburg in Washington County? We'll walk your title, explain your royalty statement, and make a straight cash offer.
heroLead: Atlasburg is a small crossroads community out past Burgettstown, and most of the mineral interests here are quiet ones, no drama, just a check that shows up or doesn't.
intro: You won't find Atlasburg marked with much more than a dot on most maps, but the ground underneath this part of Washington County has been leased and drilled for the better part of two decades. If you own minerals here, chances are the interest came down through a family farm, and the paperwork explaining exactly what you hold hasn't been touched since whoever signed the original lease.
That's the exact spot we like to start from. We ask you to send whatever you have, even if it's an old lease and a royalty check stub, and we tell you plainly what we can offer and why.

sections.heading: Small acreage, real unit exposure
paragraphs: Even a modest tract near Atlasburg can be pooled into a spacing unit that spans a section or more, meaning your royalty share is calculated against the whole unit's production rather than just what sits under your own fence line. That's standard practice in Pennsylvania's unconventional gas development, but it's rarely explained to the owner signing the original lease, and it's one of the first things we check when we review your documents.

This part of the county is squarely in the wet-gas Marcellus window, which means natural gas liquids get separated out before your royalty is calculated, and that processing step is where post-production costs typically get netted against your check.

sections.heading: Why owners here decide to sell
paragraphs: Most Atlasburg-area owners we talk to aren't chasing a windfall. They're tired of a royalty check that moves around from quarter to quarter for reasons the statement doesn't explain, or they're an out-of-state heir who inherited a fraction of a fraction and would rather have a number in hand than a quarterly mystery in the mail.
A sale converts that uncertain future income into a known amount today, and it moves the price-and-decline risk to us instead of you.

sections.heading: Confirming what you actually hold
paragraphs: Because so much of this area's mineral history traces back to farm deeds recorded well before the shale boom, we start every offer by pulling the chain of title through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds ourselves, so you're not stuck digging through courthouse records on your own.

faqs.question: I don't have a copy of my lease. Can you still make an offer?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can typically locate the recorded lease and any relevant unit designation through the county recorder's office once we know your name and the general tract location.

faqs.question: Will selling affect the operator's ability to keep producing?
faqs.answer: No. Production continues under the existing lease terms regardless of who owns the mineral interest; you're simply transferring the right to receive royalty.

faqs.question: Is there any obligation once I request an offer?
faqs.answer: None. You review the number, ask questions, and decide. There's no pressure to accept and no fee either way.
